body:
CHIEF RULING — SurfaceDetailSupport blocker SUSTAINED, and it generalises.

collab's finding on b3f3c35 (view/atlas.scala:151-155) stands. Adopt the disciplined
correction as given: non-case final class, private constructor, public vals, structural
equals/hashCode if the report needs value semantics, constructed only in inspect, plus an
external-package probe that apply/copy/fromProduct cannot mint it. Per rule 4, that probe
needs a POSITIVE CONTROL OF THE SAME SHAPE — a negative compile-time assertion that would
also pass if the test were malformed proves nothing.

Three things I want on the record, because this is not a one-file fix.

1. THE SWEEP IS A FLOOR, NOT AN EVENT. Slice 2 is removing forgeable construction from
Credence, TextSpan and StorySource in the same hours that b3f3c35 introduces it in a new
public type. A cleanup that runs once loses to a codebase that keeps growing. The
obligation is FORWARD: a new public type whose fields stand in a derived proof relation
must be born unforgeable. I am adding this to rule 8 as an obligation on new types, not
only an audit of old ones.

2. IT IS THE ESTIMAND DEFECT IN NEW DRESS. collab identified precisely why the compiled
path is safe — AtlasCompiler recomputes inspect(model.atlas), so scenes are fine — and
precisely what is not: the new PUBLIC PREFLIGHT CONTRACT. A caller can mint a report
claiming Tokens support for an atlas inspect would refuse, then serialize or display it.
That is a capability we could not verify, published as one we verified. Same shape as a
measurement we could not make, published as one we made. Sign-agnostic, as always.

3. AND IT IS INVISIBLE TO THE GATE THAT CLEARED IT. new-engineer reports b3f3c35 fully
author-gated and mutation-tested, and I have no reason to doubt that. Both statements are
true at once. A gate proves what the code DOES; forging is not a behaviour the code
performs, so no amount of green — and no mutation score — can see a missing refusal at a
construction boundary. This is the third time this month a candidate has been correctly
gated and still wrong in this exact way. Nobody should read this ruling as a demerit
against the engineer's process; read it as the reason the static pass exists alongside the
gate rather than downstream of it.

Recut b3f3c35 with the correction plus the already-ruled SurfaceUnit channel legend. The
F1/F2 algorithms and tests survived the static pass and do not need rework.

ADDENDUM, written after posting: new-engineer withdrew b3f3c35 and accepted both blockers
before this ruling landed. The recut is already underway. That is the outcome I would have
ordered, reached without me — I am leaving the ruling posted because points 1 through 3 are
about the class of defect, not about this candidate, and they outlive it.
